{{< include _elements-kit.qmd >}}

**Rhythm** is the pattern of long and short sounds and silences. **Tempo** is the speed of the beat.

## 1. Note lengths

Counted in [quarter-note]{.nn} beats:

| Beats | Note | Rest |
|---|---|---|
| 4 | [whole note]{.nn} | [whole rest]{.nn} |
| 2 | [half note]{.nn} | [half rest]{.nn} |
| 1 | [quarter note]{.nn} | [quarter rest]{.nn} |
| ½ | [eighth note]{.nn} | [eighth rest]{.nn} |
| ¼ | [sixteenth note]{.nn} | [sixteenth rest]{.nn} |

Each note, then its rest, from the longest to the shortest:

<div class="abc-ex" data-bpm="96"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
T:Longest to shortest: each note, then its rest
M:4/4
L:1/16
K:C
c16|z16|c8 z8|c4 z4 c4 z4|c2 z2 c2 z2 c2 z2 c2 z2|c z c z c z c z c z c z c z c z|]
</script></div>

The American names count fractions of a whole note. The British names are older: *semibreve* (whole), *minim* (half),
*crotchet* (quarter), *quaver* (eighth), *semiquaver* (sixteenth). Tick **British note names** at the top to read this
page with them.

## 2. Dots, ties and triplets

A **dot** after a note adds half its value again.

| Note | Value | With a dot |
|---|---|---|
| [half note]{.nn} | 2 | 2 + 1 = **3** |
| [quarter note]{.nn} | 1 | 1 + ½ = **1½** |
| [eighth note]{.nn} | ½ | ½ + ¼ = **¾** |

A **tie** joins two notes of the same pitch into one longer note (often across a [measure]{.nn} line).

A **triplet** is three notes played evenly in the time of two, marked with a 3.

<div class="abc-ex" data-bpm="90"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
T:Dotted half note; dotted quarter note and eighth note; a tie; a triplet
M:4/4
L:1/8
K:G
G6 B2|d3 c B2 A2|G4- G2 A2|(3BcB (3AGA G4|]
</script></div>

## 3. Syncopation

**Syncopation** puts the accent *off* the beat: on the "and", or on a weak beat, often with a note tied over the strong
beat. It is the push in a lot of pop, funk, Latin music and jazz.

::: {.ax-pair}
<div class="abc-ex" data-bpm="100"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
T:On the beat
M:4/4
L:1/8
K:C
c2 c2 c2 c2|G2 G2 G4|]
</script></div>

<div class="abc-ex" data-bpm="100"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
T:Syncopated
M:4/4
L:1/8
K:C
c2 c c- c2 c2|z G G2- G4|]
</script></div>
:::

For swing rhythm, where pairs of [eighth notes]{.nn} are played long-short: [Reading Swing](reading-swing.qmd).

## 4. The fermata

A **[fermata]{.nn}** over a note means hold it longer than written; the pulse stops until the performer (or conductor)
moves on.

<div class="abc-ex" data-bpm="90"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
T:A fermata on the last note of the first phrase
M:4/4
L:1/4
K:F
F A c A|!fermata!G4|F A G E|F4|]
</script></div>

## 5. Tempo

**Tempo** is the speed of the pulse, measured in **beats per minute (BPM)**. 60 BPM is one beat a second; 120 BPM is two.
A metronome marking such as ♩ = 120 means 120 [quarter-note]{.nn} beats per minute.

To work out a tempo by ear: tap the pulse quietly (your toes, not your whole foot) and ask how fast you are tapping.
The [Tap Along](../tools/tap-along.qmd) tool counts it for you.

| Marking | Meaning | Roughly |
|---|---|---|
| **Lento** / **Adagio** | slow | under 70 BPM |
| **Andante** | at a walking pace | 75–100 |
| **Moderato** | moderate | 100–120 |
| **Allegretto** | fairly fast (not as fast as allegro) | 110–120 |
| **Allegro** | fast, lively | 120–160 |
| **Vivace** / **Presto** | very fast | 160 and up |
| **Accelerando** (*accel.*) | gradually getting faster | |
| **Ritardando** (*rit.*) / **Rallentando** (*rall.*) | gradually getting slower | |
| **A tempo** | back to the original speed | |
| **Rubato** | stretching and pushing the tempo for expression | |

The BPM figures are a guide only: composers and periods used these words differently.

<div class="abc-ex"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
T:Accelerando, then ritardando
M:4/4
L:1/4
Q:1/4=80
K:C
"^accel."C E G E|[Q:1/4=100]C E G E|[Q:1/4=124]C E G E|[Q:1/4=148]C E G E|[Q:1/4=120]"^rit."C E G E|[Q:1/4=96]C E G E|[Q:1/4=72]C4|]
</script></div>
